text: Every new chat starts from nothing. Your health record should not. AI assistants give better answers from structured data. Health by Dr Brad keeps your blood tests, clinic letters, height, weight and more as one structured record, updated whenever you add to it. One file, owned only by you, in your own Dropbox or Google Drive. Every assistant, every chat, the same record. And Dr Brad's protocol behind every suggestion, with the citations. And the whole project is open source, so anyone can read exactly what it does with your data.

First, connect. In Claude, paste the connector URL. In Claude Code or Codex, one line in the terminal. Then you pick Dropbox or Google Drive. Your assistant reads and writes one file there. Nothing is stored on our server.
Put your health data, such as blood test results and clinic letters, in the Dropbox folder and ask your assistant to import them. The first time, it asks your permission to run the tool.

The file passes through Dr Brad's server and the extraction model, and is not kept. The assistant checks every value against what your record already holds: new, already recorded, or different. Nothing is filed yet.
You say yes, and the values and the letter go into the one file in your Dropbox, as structured data your assistant can use next time. Nothing is written until you say so, and nothing is ever deleted.

Ask what your plan says. It is Dr Brad's own protocol, computed from your file, with the reason and the citation behind each suggestion. Ask how any of it works and the assistant reads the code, because all of it is public.
Don't take my word for it. Paste this into ChatGPT or Claude and let it read the code. The same app also runs straight from the repository on GitHub Pages, with no server of mine at all.

Open the website and the same values are already there, because it is one file, not a copy. Change a value on the website, and your assistant sees it on its next read. Add one in the chat, and it is on the website when you refresh. Two doors, one record.
